newsitem.title: USA: Bindley Western ponders company split-up.
newsitem.headline: Bindley Western ponders company split-up.

text.p: Bindley Western Industries Inc said Friday it continues to seek ways to divide the large drug wholesaler and its Priority Healthcare subsidiary into two publicly traded companies.

"We are very enthused with the prospects for Priority Healthcare as we continue to pursue the alternatives available to divide Bindley Western and Priority into two separate public companies," said chief executive officer William Bindley in a statement.

"With a strong balance sheet and the ability to capitalize Priority to maximize expansion opportunities, we believe substantial benefits could accrue to our employees and shareholders as a result of such a transaction," Bindley said.
Bindley also said that it had elected not to proceed with closing a previously announced acquisition of Baco Drug Center Inc, a Puerto Rico-based full service drug wholesaler.
Bindley said it expects to maintain its relationship with Baco and will continue to review the benefits of the proposed acquisition as new information is received.
Bindley reported third quarter earnings rose to $0.35 a share from $0.31 a year ago. Sales increased to $1.34 billion from $1.12 billion in the third quarter last year.
